newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Palm oil imports seen rising in Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil imports seen rising in Bangladesh.

text.p: Bangladesh palm olein imports have soared in the January-November period this year compared with 1995 levels, but fell short of a 200,000 tonne target due to higher prices in the international market, traders said.

Market sources said Bangladesh's imports of crude palm olein reached 106,400 tonnes at the end of November this year and might total 120,000 tonnes in calendar 1996 against only 20,000 tonnes in 1995.
"The reduction of world oilseed production resulted in the higher price of palm olein in the international market," one importer said.
He said the price of palm olein fob per tonne in December was $560-$565 against $517 for soyabean. The price of palm olein in January would be $560 compared with $510 for soyabean, he predicted.
"The palm olein prices were more or less (equal to) soyabean until September (but) started rising in October," he said.
The importer said the price of palm olein throughout 1995 was at least $3.0 higher on average compared with soyabean in the international market.

"Palm olein imports have been rising in Bangladesh. But it all depends on the prices. You see, Bangladeshis will prefer the cheaper one," an official of the Vegetable Oil Refiners Association told Reuters.

He said Bangladeshi traders were more inclined to import palm oil mainly from Malaysia, which could be brought in within about five days in small lots. In comparison, the supply of soyabean is irregular and takes a longer time to import.
A.K.M. Fakrul Alam, country representative for Bangladesh and Burma for the Malaysian Palm Oil Promotion Council, said palm oil imports in 1997 could reach 150,000 tonnes.
"This is because of its rising demand from individuals, and producers of vanaspati, soap and detergents," he told Reuters.

But he added: "The market for palm oil remained depressed in Bangladesh because of mainly bad image and high prices. Consumers had wrongly perceived that palm oil contained high levels of fat." Alam said palm stearine, which is a substitute for tallow, was now being imported for use in producing soap and detergents.
He said his council was campaigning to promote the use of palm oil through seminars and exhibitions.
Bangladesh's total vegetable oil imports might reach 540,000 tonnes for 1996, which would include 250,000 tonnes of soyabean and 120,000 tonnes of palm olein, traders said.
They forecast total 1997 imports at about 600,000 tonnes.
The association officials said vegetable oil imports might rise by 50,000 tonnes in 1997.
Market sources said there was pressure on the government to reduce the import duty on vegetable oil to 20 percent from 30 percent, and on palm stearine to 30 percent from 45 percent.
But officials ruled out any immediate cut in duties because of the strain on the country's revenue due to falling imports.
